parsed.main_gap: Step 2 uses the false claim that a nonincreasing positive integer starting above 1 cannot reach 1; survival needs a direct argument from the move outputs.

errors.description: The claimed inference is false: a positive integer-valued nonincreasing sequence can fall from above 1 to 1. This is easily repaired because every move produces at least one entry greater than 1: if gcd(m,n)>1 it is the gcd, while if gcd(m,n)=1 the other output is mn>1.
errors.quote: A positive integer that never increases and starts above $1$ can never reach $1$; hence $P > 1$ after any number of moves.

errors.description: The final exponential-divisibility remark is imprecise or false without specifying an ordering, restricting prime support, and handling whether exponent 0 divides 0. It is not used in the proof.
errors.quote: the unique maximal $d$ with $v_p(d) \mid v_p(a_i)$ for all $p$ and all $i$.

parsed.notes: Termination and the prime-wise gcd invariant are correctly proved. With the short local repair to Step 2, both required conclusions follow completely.
